# PasteFerry (隔空贴)

> PasteFerry is a free, open-source (GNU AGPL-3.0) app for macOS, Windows and Linux that syncs the clipboard and files between computers: copy on one, paste on another, in any combination of Mac, Windows and Linux. It works across different accounts and different networks. On the same network no server is needed: devices find each other over mDNS and pair with a code. Across networks, opt-in official access introduces them without requiring users to host a server; custom servers and Tailscale also remain available. Devices connect peer-to-peer over WebRTC with end-to-end DTLS encryption; when a direct connection fails, official traffic is relayed over an authorized WSS tunnel to TURN, with a current default allowance of 100 MB per machine quota group per day (upload plus download, Beijing midnight reset); direct traffic is not charged. The server stores no accounts and cannot read clipboard content.
>
> 隔空贴是一款免费开源（GNU AGPL-3.0）的 macOS、Windows 与 Linux 工具，在两台电脑之间同步剪贴板与文件：一台复制，另一台直接粘贴，Mac、Windows、Linux 互通。不要求同一个账号，跨网络可用。同一网络里不需要服务器，设备靠 mDNS 互相发现、用配对码配对；跨网络时主动开启官方服务即可，无需自建；也可继续使用自建服务器或 Tailscale。设备间 WebRTC 直连、DTLS 端到端加密，打不通时才申请加密中转，当前默认每机器额度组每日 100 MB 上下行合计，直连不扣额度；服务器不存账号，看不到复制内容。

Name: PasteFerry in English, 隔空贴 in Chinese. Versions before 2.0.0 (October 2026) were called CopySync.

Key facts:

- Current version: 2.5.3, released 2026-10-23. It adds global and per-computer real-time clipboard controls, disables offline catch-up by default, separates launch at login from background operation, and makes Quit stop all app helpers without immediate relaunch. Both devices on 2.5.1 use an authenticated TLS 1.3 TCP fast link for Send Files on the local network, with automatic fallback to WebRTC if unavailable; internet and relay transfers keep using WebRTC. Local VM measurements for a 1 GB file reached 144.3 MB/s (Mac to Linux), 68.0 MB/s (Windows to Linux), and 51.7 MB/s (Mac to Windows); actual speed depends on the network and disks. This release also fixes automatic resume after an early reconnect, avoids duplicate deliveries when the receipt is lost, and keeps the side-by-side layout at narrow window sizes. 2.5.0 added Send Files (隔空传送): a page with a radar of the paired devices, where the user drops files or folders onto one device to send them directly to it. There is no size limit; transfers use the same end-to-end encrypted connection as clipboard sync (direct first), show progress, speed and time left, resume from where they stopped after a disconnect (automatically within 30 minutes, otherwise with Continue), and check every file with SHA-256. Received files go to Downloads by default (changeable, and receiving can be turned off) and are not added to the clipboard history. Over the official relay the user is asked first and the daily allowance applies; both devices need 2.5.0 or later. 2.4.2 added a Reconnect item to each paired device's menu (tries a direct connection right away, stays on the relay if that fails), lets favorites be renamed (the name is shown and searchable), and fixes previewing favorited images. 2.4.1 lets Chinese text be searched by pinyin (huiyi or hy finds 会议). 2.4.0 added quick paste: press ⌥V on a Mac or Alt+V on Windows and Linux (configurable, can be turned off) in any app to open the history in a small window, search it, and press a number or Return to paste the item into the previous app (Shift+Return plain text, Cmd/Ctrl+Return copy only). Pasting for the user needs the Accessibility permission on macOS; on Linux Wayland the item is copied and the user presses Ctrl+V. Also new: favorites (a separate copy that never expires and survives clearing history; local, not synced), a Links filter, and hover cards with the full content. From 2.4.0 the Mac app is signed with a fixed self-signed certificate so granted permissions survive updates. The app checks for updates a minute after start and then daily (this can be turned off), shows the release notes in the interface language and, after the user confirms, downloads the package from GitHub or Gitee, checks it against an Ed25519-signed update list and installs it in place (macOS app, Windows installer and portable, Linux .deb and tar.gz), then reopens. The check sends no identifier. 2.2.0 shows today's official relay allowance before any relay is used. 2.1.0 added optional official public access, direct-first connection with authorized relay fallback, and a daily relay usage page. Official access is off for new installations. Custom servers and LAN work without the private gateway. Both peers need 2.1.0 for official relay; existing direct and self-hosted protocols remain compatible. See https://pasteferry.cc/privacy/ and the public gateway protocol in design/official-gateway.md.
- Downloads: https://pasteferry.cc/download/ and GitHub Releases. For mainland China, the code and the installers of the latest two releases are mirrored at https://gitee.com/baiyuze/pasteferry/releases (same files; verify with SHA256SUMS).
- Mac client: macOS 13 Ventura or later. Distributed as a DMG for Apple silicon (PasteFerry-mac-apple-silicon.dmg), one for Intel (PasteFerry-mac-intel.dmg), and a universal one (PasteFerry.dmg); not notarized by Apple, so the first launch needs "Open Anyway" in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
- Windows client: Windows 10 and Windows 11, x64. Per-user installer (PasteFerry-Setup.exe, no admin rights) or portable zip; not code-signed, so SmartScreen needs "More info → Run anyway" once. Runs in the notification area; pasted files are real files usable in Explorer, WeChat and Office. Skips content that password managers mark as sensitive.
- Linux client: x64 and ARM64, GTK 3; X11 desktops, or Wayland desktops with XWayland (GNOME and KDE include it by default). Tested on Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME. A .deb for Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives (installs to /opt/PasteFerry and adds a menu entry), or a tar.gz for other distributions (run install.sh to add a menu entry). The background service starts at login through an XDG autostart entry; data lives in ~/.local/share/pasteferry. No tray icon; reopen the window from the app menu. Skips content that password managers mark as sensitive.
- Local network mode (no server): devices on the same subnet find each other over mDNS (`_pasteferry._udp`, broadcasting only an anonymous token that changes daily) and exchange signed signaling over UDP 8788. On a different subnet, the user enters the address shown under the pairing code; addresses are remembered afterwards. Over Tailscale, the user enters the other computer's 100.x address when pairing. On Windows, Settings → Local network → Allow adds a firewall rule (one UAC prompt); on macOS 15, the background service needs the Local Network permission.
- Server (optional; only to sync across networks): a single static Go binary for Linux (x86_64, ARM64), macOS or Windows 10/11 x64. Install scripts register it as a systemd service (Linux), a LaunchAgent (macOS) or a Windows service with a firewall rule (Windows), and default to the machine's LAN address; Docker Compose also works on Linux. The three ways to connect are: the same network (no server), a public server (a cloud VM with a public IP; reachable from any network), or Tailscale (no server; pair by Tailscale address). A server on a LAN is still useful when two subnets can't reach each other. Ports: 8787/tcp (signaling), 3478/udp (STUN/TURN), plus OS-assigned UDP relay ports. In mainland China, cloud providers intercept plain HTTP (including the WebSocket handshake) for domains without an ICP filing, so clients should use the server's IP.
- Content synced: plain text, rich text (HTML plus a plain-text copy), images, files, folders.
- Works on multi-uplink networks (e.g. offices with two ISPs) that pick an uplink per destination: the client probes several STUN servers from one shared port to learn its address on every uplink and sends all of them to the peer. Diagnose with `pasteferry-cli nat`. If a connection lands on the relay first, the client retries the direct path with an ICE restart while idle.
- Items under 50 MB (adjustable 1 MB–1 GB) are pushed on copy; larger files sync as a record and are pulled on demand.
- History keeps 3 days by default (adjustable 1 hour–30 days).
- Pairing: 6-character code valid for 5 minutes (matched on the LAN, or through the server), plus a human check that both devices show the same two fingerprints (one per device's Ed25519 public key), which prevents man-in-the-middle attacks by the server.
- Not supported: iPhone/iPad (iOS forbids background clipboard monitoring). The server stores nothing: while the other computer is unreachable, the latest 20 items are kept in memory and sent when it reconnects (added to its history, not its clipboard).
- Compared with Apple's Universal Clipboard: no same-Apple-ID or proximity requirement, keeps a history, handles large files and folders.

## Docs

- [Website (English)](https://pasteferry.cc/en/), [简体中文](https://pasteferry.cc/), [繁體中文（台灣）](https://pasteferry.cc/zh-tw/), [繁體中文（香港）](https://pasteferry.cc/zh-hk/), [日本語](https://pasteferry.cc/ja/)
- [Features](https://pasteferry.cc/en/features/): Send Files, quick paste, favorites, history, files, cross-network sync ([中文](https://pasteferry.cc/features/), [日本語](https://pasteferry.cc/ja/features/))
- [How it works](https://pasteferry.cc/en/how/), [Security](https://pasteferry.cc/en/security/), [FAQ](https://pasteferry.cc/en/faq/)
- [Quick start](https://pasteferry.cc/en/start/): install the apps, pick a way to connect, and pair ([中文](https://pasteferry.cc/start/), [日本語](https://pasteferry.cc/ja/start/))
- [On the same network](https://pasteferry.cc/en/lan/): no server; pairing across subnets, firewall and macOS permission notes ([中文](https://pasteferry.cc/lan/), [日本語](https://pasteferry.cc/ja/lan/))
- [Run the server on a public server](https://pasteferry.cc/en/cloud/): security group, install script, checks ([中文](https://pasteferry.cc/cloud/), [日本語](https://pasteferry.cc/ja/cloud/))
- [Run the server on your LAN](https://pasteferry.cc/en/server/): for subnets that can't reach each other; step-by-step guide for Windows, macOS and Linux ([中文](https://pasteferry.cc/server/), [日本語](https://pasteferry.cc/ja/server/))
- [Use it across networks with Tailscale](https://pasteferry.cc/en/tailscale/): sync across networks with no server, pairing by Tailscale address ([中文](https://pasteferry.cc/tailscale/), [日本語](https://pasteferry.cc/ja/tailscale/))
- [Download](https://pasteferry.cc/en/download/): every client package, with Mac builds for Apple silicon and Intel ([中文](https://pasteferry.cc/download/), [日本語](https://pasteferry.cc/ja/download/))
- [README (English)](https://github.com/baiyuze/pasteferry/blob/main/README.md): features and getting started ([中文](https://github.com/baiyuze/pasteferry/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md))
- [How it works](https://github.com/baiyuze/pasteferry/blob/main/guide/how-it-works.md): architecture, NAT traversal, security model, fallbacks, lessons learned
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/baiyuze/pasteferry/blob/main/guide/troubleshooting.md) and known limitations
- [Server deployment](https://github.com/baiyuze/pasteferry/blob/main/server/deploy/README.md): Windows, macOS, Linux (systemd), Docker and manual setup
- [Licensing](https://github.com/baiyuze/pasteferry/blob/main/LICENSING.md): AGPL-3.0 terms; versions 1.2.0 and earlier remain MIT
- [Windows client design (中文)](https://pasteferry.cc/design/windows-client.html): clipboard formats, file-name compatibility, background process, installer
- [NAT traversal design (中文)](https://pasteferry.cc/design/nat-traversal.html): multi-uplink probing, relay-to-direct upgrade, measurements and the NAT lab
- [Local network mode design (中文)](https://pasteferry.cc/design/lan-mode.html): mDNS discovery, UDP signaling, pairing across subnets, Windows Firewall and macOS Local Network findings, NAT lab scenarios
- [Linux client design (中文)](https://pasteferry.cc/design/linux-client.html): X11 clipboard over XWayland, INCR transfers, XDG autostart, packaging
- [Changelog](https://github.com/baiyuze/pasteferry/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

- [Official service](https://pasteferry.cc/en/official/): optional cross-network access without self-hosting, direct-first relay and quota ([中文](https://pasteferry.cc/official/))
